# E019 -- Adobe

## Metadata
- **Brand:** Adobe (legal entity: Adobe Inc.)
- **Industry:** Technology / Creative Software
- **Year:** 2018 (November)
- **Document type:** Internal corporate brand guidelines (marked "Adobe Confidential")
- **Source file:** adobe-brand_guidelines.pdf
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13, 25-30, 39-42, 66-70
- **Total pages:** 74

## Brand Strategy
- Mission-driven brand built around five personality tenets: Clean, Community, Captivating, Forward, Inspiring.
- "Clean" tenet emphasises simplicity, getting out of the user's way, limiting superlatives and hyperbole.
- "Community" tenet stresses co-creation, attribution, two-way dialogue, championing user work.
- Brand voice is singular and consistent regardless of audience -- "content changes; voice doesn't."
- Strong legal naming discipline: must always be "Adobe" (never "Adobe Systems" or variants).

## Logo
- Two logo families: Standard Adobe logos and Red Tag Adobe logos.
- As of May 2014, all logos updated to use Adobe Clean typeface.
- As of September 2013, no legal (R) symbol on logo; legal attribution required separately.
- Red tag logos reserved for specific corporate contexts.
- Detailed incorrect-use examples provided (page 23).
- Logo examples given across contexts: print, online, events, facilities, non-standard, third-party use.

## Typography
- **Primary typeface:** Adobe Clean (proprietary to Adobe, not available for partner or public license).
- Weights: Light, Regular, Bold, SemiCondensed, and corresponding italics.
- Detailed tracking table by point size (e.g. 4pt = +20, 9pt+ = 0, 14pt = -3, 36pt = -8).
- Auto or metric kerning recommended.
- Alternate glyphs available for "g" and "1".
- **CJK support:** Adobe Clean Han (Japanese, Korean, Simplified/Traditional Chinese).
- **Serif fallback:** Adobe Clean Serif -- available by request, rarely used, mainly for lengthy legal content.
- Red text colour is prohibited (reserved for corporate logo).

## Color
- Open colour system -- no defined corporate palette beyond red.
- Colours categorised as "dynamic" and "neutral"; always pair dynamic + neutral, never all one type.
- **Red:** Elevated to special status, reserved primarily for the corporate mark. Must not be used as primary colour on materials or as text colour.
- Product colours are defined separately in product-specific brand guides.

## Graphics / Illustration
- Conceptual illustration curated to be current; Adobe positions itself as a standard-bearer for illustrators.
- Infographics system with defined components: anatomy, graphs/charts, iconography, typography, and colour palette.
- Product logotypes: styled consistently in all-black or all-white; red+black product name treatment discontinued.
- "Design advantage imagery" used for conceptual communications.

## Photography
- Reportage style with three categories: Atmospheric (spaces/details), Depersonalized (people not primary focus), Personal (captured in a moment, never posed).
- Natural light, genuine engagement, mix of colour and black-and-white.
- Environment as hero rather than the individual.
- Avoid literal visual metaphors.
- When using multiple photos: mix all types, never pair same emotion + same camera angle; juxtaposition should tell a bigger story.
- Stock photography must be from Adobe Stock and requires brand review before licensing.

## Applications
- Email signatures, presentation templates, stationery all templated.
- Branded merchandise: wearables, gifts -- specific rules for code/team names on merch.
- Adobe Sensei sub-brand: no logo/icon, always uses "Adobe Sensei" (never just "Sensei"), "Powered by Adobe Sensei" ingredient brand for AI/ML features.

## Tone of Voice
- Conversational, direct, confident, bold but not boastful.
- Expects intelligence from audience; avoids lowest-common-denominator communication.
- Peer-to-peer tone focusing on real-world value over technical features.
- Passion for technology balanced by understanding that innovation is meaningless without customer benefit.
- Separate "Tactical Guide for Writers" provides deeper editorial guidance (Asset ID 212406).
- Headline punctuation rules documented.

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- Deliberately open colour system (no defined palette) is unusual for a major tech brand -- relies on creative judgment.
- Detailed tracking tables for typography at every point size is rarely seen in brand guidelines.
- Document explicitly marks confidential/internal status, yet functions as a comprehensive external-grade guideline.
- The separation of photography into three named categories (Atmospheric, Depersonalized, Personal) is a strong editorial framework.
- Adobe Sensei sub-brand guidelines include a qualification council process for AI feature claims.

## Quality Score
5 / 5 -- Exceptionally comprehensive across all brand dimensions. 74 pages covering strategy, personality tenets, logo variants with usage context, proprietary typeface with detailed specifications, photography philosophy with clear categories, voice guidelines with examples, legal guidelines, templates, and merchandise rules. One of the most thorough corporate brand systems in this collection.
